description: The original Windows-only implementation of .NET, versions 1.0 to 4.8.1, installed as part of Windows and no longer receiving new features.
.NET 5 and later (today .NET 10), the cross-platform line that grew out of .NET Core and receives all new features.
The support model of .NET Framework 4.5.2 and later: a version is supported for as long as the Windows version it is installed on.
The token in a project file that names the target, such as `net48`, `netstandard2.0` or `net10.0`.
The short `.csproj` format that starts with `<Project Sdk="...">`, uses `PackageReference` and is required by modern .NET.
The last API specification implemented by .NET Framework, used for libraries shared between a .NET Framework app and a modern .NET app.
Building one project for several TFMs with `<TargetFrameworks>`, branching code with symbols such as `NETFRAMEWORK` and `NET10_0_OR_GREATER`.
